description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh, late 50s, one-eyed (blind in left eye from smallpox), long grey beard tied up, saffron and gold silk robe, jewelled kalgi and turban with an emerald aigrette, seated regal bearing, shrewd commanding expression, early 19th-century Sikh court dress

Hari Singh Nalwa, powerful Sikh general in his 40s, thick black beard, dark blue and gold Khalsa battle turban with steel quoit, chainmail and steel armour over robes, sword and shield, stern martial gaze, early 19th-century Khalsa Army

Sham Singh Attariwala, veteran Sikh general in his 50s, long flowing white beard, white robes and white turban, saffron sash, mounted-warrior bearing, resolute weathered expression, early 19th-century Sikh commander

Akali Phula Singh, Nihang warrior-ascetic in his 50s, dense grey beard, towering conical blue dumalla turban stacked with steel chakrams and a khanda, dark blue Nihang robes, fierce zealous eyes, early 19th-century irregular commander

Zorawar Singh Kahluria, Dogra mountain general in his 40s, black beard, fur-trimmed Himalayan cloak over armour, red and gold turban, hardy weather-beaten face, snow-campaign bearing, early 19th-century mountain warfare

Maharani Jind Kaur, regent queen in her 30s, elegant, dark hair veiled with a fine embroidered dupatta, gold nose ring and heavy jewellery, rich crimson and gold silks, proud defiant expression, 19th-century Sikh royal woman

Maharaja Duleep Singh as restored young ruler, mid 20s, neat dark beard, jewelled turban with a large pearl and emerald aigrette, sky-blue and gold court robe, pearl necklaces, youthful dignified expression, mid 19th-century Lahore court
Master Tara Singh, Akali leader in his 50s, long grey beard, plain black-and-white turban, simple dark achkan, spectacles, intense oratorical expression, 1930s-40s Sikh nationalist
Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan, Punjabi Muslim statesman in his 40s, neat moustache and short beard, karakul cap, dark sherwani with watch chain, dignified premier's bearing, 1930s-40s Punjab Unionist

Sir Khizar Hayat Khan Tiwana, Punjabi Muslim landowner-politician in his late 30s, trimmed moustache, karakul cap, western suit under a formal coat, composed measured expression, 1940s Unionist premier
Sir Chhotu Ram, stocky Jat peasant leader in his 50s, clean-shaven with heavy moustache, plain white turban and homespun kurta, earnest agrarian-reformer expression, 1930s-40s rural Punjab
Sardar Baldev Singh, Sikh Panthic politician in his 40s, dark beard neatly rolled, well-tied navy turban, dark western suit with tie, businesslike confident expression, 1940s Punjab
Lala Har Dayal, revolutionary intellectual in his 50s, thin face, small moustache, dark hair swept back, plain dark jacket over kurta, austere scholarly-radical expression, 1930s Ghadar ideologue
Sohan Singh Bhakna, elder Ghadar leader in his 60s, long white beard, plain white turban and coarse kurta, weathered dignified peasant-revolutionary expression, 1930s-40s Punjab

Bhagat Singh, young revolutionary in his early 20s, clean-shaven with a curled upturned moustache, tilted felt trilby hat, plain shirt and jacket, defiant fearless expression, iconic 1930s Lahore revolutionary-socialist
